tail:
Step 6b is done for batches 1–3. Report: `research/frontier-15-alpha-a-6b.md`.

## Three fatal defects, all in batch 2, none raised by the reader

**`thm-sylow-first-theorem`** — a landmark with 14 in-batch consumers. Two of its four steps announced a method instead of arguing: step 3.1 was, in full, *"We apply induction to that stabilizer."* Both load-bearing inferences were missing (why the stabilizer is proper unless $G$ is a $p$-group; why the induction hypothesis applies to it). I rewrote the proof and verified the route by extracting text from the source PDFs — Idelhaj §3, the stated locator, carries exactly this Wielandt action, and its Lemma 3.6 *is* the batch's binomial-valuation lemma. Also corrected the item's reference, which pointed at Conrad's *Consequences* note, which doesn't prove Sylow I.

**Two undeclared choice principles** — `thm-composition-series-iff-noetherian-and-artinian` (dependent choice) and `thm-finitely-generated-nonzero-modules-have-maximal-proper-submodules` (Zorn), both with unconditional Statements and titles over proofs that name the principle outright. Reader 2 declared this exact class fatal twice in the same batch and reader 3 fifteen times in batch 3; these were missed. I scoped DC to the converse direction only, confirmed from disk that neither consumer inherits it, and propagated the AC hypothesis into one consumer's fact restatement.

Once the class appeared twice I wrote a detector rather than hand-reading. Three hits, one a false positive I confirmed is genuinely choice-free.

## A systemic non-disposition class

15 items closed with steps like *"We include the trivial group and the one-prime case"* — naming boundary cases and checking none. Two were leaked authoring instructions. I evaluated every named case before repairing; all were true this time. The mechanism is the finding: the contract's boundary evidence was built by **quoting the proof's final step**, so an announcement and its boundary row were the same non-disposition twice, and `boundary-audit`'s template detector can't cluster them because each is worded differently. 32 rows re-anchored with per-case evidence.

## Two things I want to flag

**No independent refutation happened.** The Sol refuter lane is quota-locked until 2026-08-20; I probed it rather than trusting group `b`'s earlier failure. I did the adversarial reading myself and did not substitute another model. Nobody has adversarially read the Sylow I proof I wrote.

**I wrote 33 of 125 risk reviews and left 92 blank on purpose.** With no refuter, the only basis for one is my own reading, and I didn't read those 92 to that standard — batch 3 I audited through reader 3's report plus one deep verification of its riskiest repair, not item by item. Writing them to clear `--require-reviewed` would turn an honest red into a false green. **The gate stays red on 92 items.**

Also open: `finite-smoke` registers zero obligations across all 172 proof-bearing items — it runs, exits zero, and checks nothing, in batches full of Sylow counts and explicit finite witnesses. Logged as `open` for the lead Alpha.

All gates green after repair (contract/fidelity/boundary 0 errors on all three batches, content-policy 207/207, 324 items precheck clean, 22/22 source URLs live). 8 defect-ledger rows written alongside their dispositions. Batches 1–3 are materially better, but not clear for step 7 on my attestation alone.
